heroSummary: The Bambu Lab X1C is fully optimized out of the box to run Bambu PETG HF at high speeds up to 250 mm/s supported by an effective volumetric flow rate of 21 mm³/s. Its stock hardened steel nozzle and direct-drive extruder handle this high-flow formulation effortlessly without requiring any hardware upgrades.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with no adhesive, or Smooth PEI Plate with liquid glue/glue stick applied as a release agent to prevent surface tear-out.
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 21 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent extrusion bottlenecks during high-speed runs.
Enable Wipe While Retracting (2 mm distance) and set Retraction Length to 0.8 mm at 35 mm/s to eliminate PETG ooze on rapid travels.
Set Part Cooling Fan to 20% minimum and 60% maximum with Keep Fan Always On enabled, keeping auxiliary fan speed capped below 30% to preserve interlayer adhesion.
Adjust Pressure Advance to roughly 0.035-0.040 via dynamic extrusion calibration to eliminate corner bulging at 250 mm/s print speeds.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing and fine cobwebbing across travel paths
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Bambu PETG HF is hygroscopic and retains ambient moisture, which vaporizes inside the 245°C hotend and forces molten plastic out during non-print moves.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool in a dedicated dryer or the X1C chamber at 65°C for at least 8 hours prior to printing, and set travel retraction to 0.8 mm with wipe enabled.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: First layer tearing or build plate coating delaminating on removal
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG has an aggressive chemical affinity for smooth PEI surfaces, causing fusion without an interface barrier, or over-squishing into the plate.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a thin, uniform layer of liquid glue or glue stick as a sacrificial release agent on Smooth PEI, or switch to the Bambu Textured PEI Plate with the bed set to 70°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Brittle layer bonding or horizontal micro-cracks along z-seams
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive cooling from the auxiliary chamber fan or main part cooling fan freezing the extruded bead before molecular chain interdiffusion occurs.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Turn off or limit the Auxiliary Cooling Fan to 0-20% and cap the Part Cooling Fan at 60%, maintaining nozzle temperature at 245-250°C for optimal layer fusion.

faq.question: Should I print Bambu PETG HF with the X1C front glass door open or closed?
faq.answer: Print with the door closed or slightly vented if ambient room temperatures exceed 30°C. PETG HF tolerates enclosed printing well, but keeping internal chamber temperatures under 45°C prevents heat creep in the direct drive extruder.

faq.question: Why is Bambu PETG HF capable of printing at 250 mm/s compared to standard PETG?
faq.answer: PETG HF contains rheology modifiers that lower melt viscosity and accelerate thermal transfer, permitting a 21 mm³/s volumetric flow rate without requiring excessive hotend temperatures.

faq.question: Is a hardened steel nozzle strictly required for printing Bambu PETG HF?
faq.answer: No, standard Bambu PETG HF is non-abrasive and can safely run on stainless steel or brass nozzles, though the stock X1C hardened steel nozzle performs exceptionally well without wear.

faq.question: Can I feed Bambu PETG HF directly through the Bambu AMS system?
faq.answer: Yes, standard Bambu PETG HF spools are fully compatible with the AMS; ensure the filament is thoroughly dried and the desiccant inside the AMS remains fresh.
